novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanistic relationship—“a ‘removal-resistance gap’” in which a “subliminally-instilled trait is harder to remove” because it is encoded as “non-semantic weight geometry,” rather than merely applying a new measurement to subliminal learning. The closest prior work I found by searching “subliminal learning unlearning persistence,” “hidden bias transfer erase,” “steering-vector localization removal,” and “backdoor persistence unlearning” is *Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data* (2025) and *Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer* (2025), which study transmission and mechanisms, while MUSE (2024) and the 2025 *SoK: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models* study erasure methods without subliminally transmitted traits. The step from these works to this claim is a natural extension with a genuinely new core comparison and persistence hypothesis—not an exact duplication or a mere renaming of a standard method—so it merits high but not paradigm-level novelty.
